meta.title: Literature Review Summaries: Heart Disease Prediction using Ensemble Learning
meta.author: Salil Mahale (Roll 53, PID 232085), BE CMPN B, Batch 3
meta.affil: Machine Learning [CSL 701] mini project, guide Dr. Nazneen Ansari
meta.email: St. Francis Institute of Technology, University of Mumbai, 2026-27
meta.keywords: heart disease, ensemble learning, literature review

abstract: Twenty verified research papers (2018 to 2025) on machine learning and ensemble methods for heart disease prediction, summarised with dataset, technique, reported result and relevance to the MPBE re-implementation.

blocks.text: This document summarises the twenty research papers reviewed for the mini project on heart disease prediction using ensemble learning. Reference numbers match the References chapter of the report and the paper; [1] is the base paper that was re-implemented.
Base paper
[1] Prediction of Heart Disease using Ensemble Learning (Muthulakshmi, Parveen and Rajeswari, 2023)

**Dataset:** UCI Cleveland, 303 records, 14 attributes. **Technique:** MinMax normalisation, Pearson correlation feature selection, and a bagging ensemble (100 estimators) with Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naive Bayes and SVM as base classifiers, aggregated by mean score under k-fold cross validation; individual baselines DT 81.66%, RF 83.33%, NB 88.33%, SVM 90%. **Reported result:** proposed MPBE 95.33% accuracy, claimed 2 to 9 points above stratified k-fold, soft voting, GAE-RF AdaBoost, AB-WAE and SEIML. **Our reading:** the correlation threshold and the aggregation rule are not stated, scaling and selection appear to be applied to the whole dataset before splitting, and only accuracy is reported. These gaps are what our re-implementation makes explicit.
Reviewed papers
[2] Risk prediction of cardiovascular disease using ML classifiers (2022)

**Full reference:** M. Pal, S. Parija, G. Panda, K. Dhama and R. K. Mohapatra, "Risk prediction of cardiovascular disease using machine learning classifiers," Open Medicine, vol. 17, no. 1, pp. 1100-1113, 2022. doi: 10.1515/med-2022-0508
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Multilayer Perceptron and K-Nearest Neighbour
**Reported result:** MLP 82.47% accuracy, AUC 86.41%

**Summary:** Pal et al. compared a neural classifier and a distance based classifier on the Cleveland data after standard preprocessing. The MLP was the stronger of the two, and the authors framed the work as a decision support aid for early screening.
**Relevance to this project:** Establishes the roughly 80 to 85 percent accuracy band that single classifiers reach on Cleveland, which is the baseline our ensembles must beat.
[3] Cardiovascular disease detection using ensemble learning (2022)

**Full reference:** A. Alqahtani, S. Alsubai, M. Sha, L. Vilcekova and T. Javed, "Cardiovascular Disease Detection using Ensemble Learning," Computational Intelligence and Neuroscience, vol. 2022, art. 5267498, pp. 1-9, 2022. doi: 10.1155/2022/5267498
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Random Forest, KNN, Decision Tree, XGBoost plus a stacked ensemble and K-modes clustering
**Reported result:** Stacked model reported 88.7% accuracy
**Summary:** Alqahtani et al. trained several tree based learners and combined them through stacking. They also used clustering to study structure in the patient population before classification.
**Relevance to this project:** Directly comparable to our Stacking model; supports our finding that stacking is among the strongest ensembles on Cleveland.
[4] An improved ensemble learning approach for heart disease risk (2020)

**Full reference:** I. D. Mienye, Y. Sun and Z. Wang, "An improved ensemble learning approach for the prediction of heart disease risk," Informatics in Medicine Unlocked, vol. 20, art. 100402, 2020. doi: 10.1016/j.imu.2020.100402
**Dataset:** Cleveland and Framingham
**Technique:** Homogeneous ensemble of CART trees combined by an accuracy based weighted aging classifier
**Reported result:** 93% on Cleveland, 91% on Framingham

**Summary:** Mienye, Sun and Wang partitioned the training data randomly, trained one CART model per partition and combined them with weights that depend on each model's accuracy. Weaker members were aged out.
**Relevance to this project:** Shows that a homogeneous bagging style ensemble with a smarter aggregation rule can beat plain majority voting; motivates our soft (mean probability) aggregation.
[5] A hybrid intelligent system framework for heart disease prediction (2018)

**Full reference:** A. U. Haq, J. P. Li, M. H. Memon, S. Nazir and R. Sun, "A Hybrid Intelligent System Framework for the Prediction of Heart Disease Using Machine Learning Algorithms," Mobile Information Systems, vol. 2018, art. 3860146, pp. 1-21, 2018. doi: 10.1155/2018/3860146
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Seven classifiers (LR, KNN, ANN, SVM, NB, DT, RF) with Relief, mRMR and LASSO feature selection under 10-fold CV
**Reported result:** Logistic Regression with Relief features 89% accuracy

**Summary:** Haq et al. is one of the most cited feature selection studies on this dataset. They showed that reducing the 13 attributes to a relevant subset both cut computation and improved accuracy for most classifiers.
**Relevance to this project:** Our Pearson selection step follows the same principle with a simpler, correlation based filter; their 10-fold protocol is the one we adopt.
[6] A reliable machine intelligence model using ensemble techniques (2022)

**Full reference:** B. P. Doppala, D. Bhattacharyya, M. Janarthanan and N. Baik, "A Reliable Machine Intelligence Model for Accurate Identification of Cardiovascular Diseases Using Ensemble Techniques," Journal of Healthcare Engineering, vol. 2022, art. 2585235, 2022. doi: 10.1155/2022/2585235
**Dataset:** Cleveland, Statlog and a Mendeley cardiovascular dataset
**Technique:** Majority voting and stacking ensembles with GridSearch tuned base learners
**Reported result:** Up to 96% accuracy on the combined data
**Summary:** Doppala et al. evaluated ensembles on more than one heart dataset and argued that reliability requires agreement across datasets, not a single high score.
**Relevance to this project:** Their multi dataset design is the direct motivation for our second, combined 5 source dataset.
[7] Robust heart disease prediction based on significant features and ensemble learning (2020)

**Full reference:** M. A. Alim, S. Habib, Y. Farooq and A. Rafay, "Robust Heart Disease Prediction: A Novel Approach based on Significant Feature and Ensemble learning Model," in Proc. 3rd Int. Conf. on Computing, Mathematics and Engineering Technologies (iCoMET), 2020, pp. 1-5. doi: 10.1109/iCoMET48670.2020.9074135
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Correlation based feature selection followed by an ensemble of Random Forest, SVM and Naive Bayes
**Reported result:** Ensemble 86.8% accuracy versus 82 to 84% for the base learners
**Summary:** Alim et al. removed weakly correlated attributes and then combined heterogeneous base learners; the ensemble improved over every individual model.
**Relevance to this project:** Very close in spirit to MPBE (correlation filter plus heterogeneous ensemble); their accuracy is in line with what we reproduce.
[8] Effective heart disease prediction using hybrid ML techniques (HRFLM) (2019)

**Full reference:** S. Mohan, C. Thirumalai and G. Srivastava, "Effective Heart Disease Prediction Using Hybrid Machine Learning Techniques," IEEE Access, vol. 7, pp. 81542-81554, 2019. doi: 10.1109/ACCESS.2019.2923707
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Hybrid Random Forest with a Linear Model over selected feature combinations
**Reported result:** 88.7% accuracy
**Summary:** Mohan, Thirumalai and Srivastava searched over feature subsets and combined a random forest with a linear model. The paper is widely used as a benchmark for Cleveland.
**Relevance to this project:** Provides the most common reference accuracy (88.7%) that later papers, including ours, compare against.
[9] Improving accuracy of heart disease risk prediction with ensemble classification (2019)

**Full reference:** C. B. C. Latha and S. C. Jeeva, "Improving the accuracy of prediction of heart disease risk based on ensemble classification techniques," Informatics in Medicine Unlocked, vol. 16, art. 100203, 2019. doi: 10.1016/j.imu.2019.100203
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Bagging, boosting, stacking and majority voting over NB, C4.5, MLP, PART and RF, with and without feature selection
**Reported result:** Majority vote improved weak classifiers by up to 7.26%

**Summary:** Latha and Jeeva quantified how much each ensemble family lifts a weak base learner. Voting gave the largest gain, bagging and boosting slightly less, and feature selection added a further small improvement.
**Relevance to this project:** The clearest evidence that ensemble gains over weak learners are large but gains over already strong learners are small, which matches our results.
[10] Early detection of coronary heart disease using ensemble techniques (2021)
**Full reference:** V. Shorewala, "Early detection of coronary heart disease using ensemble techniques," Informatics in Medicine Unlocked, vol. 26, art. 100655, 2021. doi: 10.1016/j.imu.2021.100655
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Bagging, boosting and stacking compared with tuned single models
**Reported result:** Stacked ensemble of KNN, RF and SVM best at about 75% accuracy
**Summary:** Shorewala found that stacking outperformed bagging and boosting once base learners were tuned, but also that absolute accuracy on this small dataset stayed modest.
**Relevance to this project:** Cautions against expecting very high accuracies on Cleveland; supports our decision to report cross validated rather than single split scores.
[11] Heart disease prediction using supervised ML: performance analysis and comparison (2021)

**Full reference:** M. M. Ali, B. K. Paul, K. Ahmed, F. M. Bui, J. M. W. Quinn and M. A. Moni, "Heart disease prediction using supervised machine learning algorithms: Performance analysis and comparison," Computers in Biology and Medicine, vol. 136, art. 104672, 2021. doi: 10.1016/j.compbiomed.2021.104672
**Dataset:** Kaggle heart dataset
**Technique:** KNN, DT and RF with feature importance analysis
**Reported result:** RF reported 100% on a leaky Kaggle copy of the data

**Summary:** Ali et al. reported perfect scores for Random Forest. Later analyses attribute such results to duplicated rows in the Kaggle version of the dataset, which makes test rows appear in training.
**Relevance to this project:** A warning about duplicates and leakage; it is why we de duplicate the combined dataset (1190 to 918 rows) and fit scaling inside each CV fold.
[12] Heart disease prediction using ML techniques (2020)

**Full reference:** D. Shah, S. Patel and S. K. Bharti, "Heart Disease Prediction using Machine Learning Techniques," SN Computer Science, vol. 1, no. 6, art. 345, 2020. doi: 10.1007/s42979-020-00365-y
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, KNN and Random Forest
**Reported result:** KNN best at 90.8% accuracy on one split
**Summary:** Shah, Patel and Bharti gave a compact comparison of four classical classifiers and a description of the 14 attributes that many student projects reuse.
**Relevance to this project:** Useful as a plain language description of the attributes; its single split protocol explains why its numbers are higher than cross validated ones.
[13] Prediction of heart disease using a combination of ML and deep learning (2021)

**Full reference:** R. Bharti, A. Khamparia, M. Shabaz, G. Dhiman, S. Pande and P. Singh, "Prediction of Heart Disease Using a Combination of Machine Learning and Deep Learning," Computational Intelligence and Neuroscience, vol. 2021, art. 8387680, pp. 1-11, 2021. doi: 10.1155/2021/8387680
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Isolation Forest outlier removal, LASSO feature selection, classical ML and a deep neural network
**Reported result:** Deep learning 94.2% accuracy
**Summary:** Bharti et al. tested three pipelines (no selection, selection, selection plus outlier removal) and found the deep model benefited most from cleaning.
**Relevance to this project:** Shows that preprocessing choices move results by several points; we keep preprocessing minimal and explicit so the effect of the ensemble itself is visible.
[14] Ensemble methods for heart disease prediction (2021)
**Full reference:** T. Karadeniz, G. Tokdemir and H. H. Maras, "Ensemble Methods for Heart Disease Prediction," New Generation Computing, vol. 39, no. 3, pp. 569-581, 2021.
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Bagging, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest and stacking
**Reported result:** Ensembles outperformed single learners; boosting and stacking strongest
**Summary:** Karadeniz, Tokdemir and Maras compared the main ensemble families head to head on the same data and preprocessing.
**Relevance to this project:** The same family comparison we perform; our AdaBoost and Stacking results agree with theirs on Cleveland.
[15] Heart disease identification using ML classification in e-healthcare (2020)

**Full reference:** J. P. Li, A. U. Haq, S. U. Din, J. Khan, A. Khan and A. Saboor, "Heart Disease Identification Method Using Machine Learning Classification in E-Healthcare," IEEE Access, vol. 8, pp. 107562-107582, 2020.
**Dataset:** Cleveland (UCI)
**Technique:** Feature selection (Relief, mRMR, LASSO and a proposed FCMIM) with SVM, LR, ANN, KNN, DT and NB
**Reported result:** SVM with FCMIM selected features 92.37% accuracy
**Summary:** Li et al. proposed a conditional mutual information based selector and reported that a linear SVM on the selected features gave the best result.
**Relevance to this project:** Another feature selection study on the same 13 attributes; supports keeping exang, cp, oldpeak, thal and ca, which our Pearson filter also keeps.
[16] Optimized ensemble learning with explainable AI for heart disease prediction (2024)

**Full reference:** I. D. Mienye and N. Jere, "Optimized Ensemble Learning Approach with Explainable AI for Improved Heart Disease Prediction," Information, vol. 15, no. 7, art. 394, 2024. doi: 10.3390/info15070394
**Dataset:** Cleveland and Framingham
**Technique:** Random Forest, AdaBoost and XGBoost tuned with Bayesian optimization, explained with SHAP
**Reported result:** XGBoost 97.1% on Cleveland, 92.1% on Framingham
**Summary:** Mienye and Jere tuned three ensembles with Bayesian optimization and used SHAP to explain predictions to clinicians, arguing that accuracy alone does not lead to clinical adoption.
**Relevance to this project:** Motivates our feature importance analysis (chapter 6) and is the most recent strong ensemble benchmark on Cleveland.
[17] Enhancing heart disease prediction with ensemble learning and hyperparameter optimization (2023)

**Full reference:** D. Asif, M. Bibi, M. S. Arif and A. Mukheimer, "Enhancing Heart Disease Prediction through Ensemble Learning Techniques with Hyperparameter Optimization," Algorithms, vol. 16, no. 6, art. 308, 2023. doi: 10.3390/a16060308
**Dataset:** Three merged Kaggle heart datasets
**Technique:** Extra Trees, RF, XGBoost and CatBoost with GridSearchCV
**Reported result:** Extra Trees 98.15% accuracy on an 80:20 split
**Summary:** Asif et al. merged datasets with the same attributes to obtain a larger training set and then tuned ensemble hyperparameters with grid search.
**Relevance to this project:** Their merged dataset approach is the closest published analogue of our combined 5 source dataset.
[18] Enhancing heart disease prediction accuracy through ML and optimization (2023)

**Full reference:** N. Chandrasekhar and S. Peddakrishna, "Enhancing Heart Disease Prediction Accuracy through Machine Learning Techniques and Optimization," Processes, vol. 11, no. 4, art. 1210, 2023. doi: 10.3390/pr11041210
**Dataset:** Cleveland and IEEE Dataport
**Technique:** RF, KNN, LR, NB, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost and a soft voting ensemble tuned with GridSearchCV
**Reported result:** Soft voting 95% on IEEE Dataport, LR 90.16% on Cleveland
**Summary:** Chandrasekhar and Peddakrishna tuned six learners with five fold grid search and found that a soft voting ensemble of the tuned models improved both datasets.
**Relevance to this project:** Their soft voting ensemble corresponds to our Voting (soft) model and supports probability averaging over hard voting.
[19] Efficient medical diagnosis of heart diseases with and without GridSearchCV (2022)

**Full reference:** G. N. Ahmad, H. Fatima, S. Ullah, A. S. Saidi and Imdadullah, "Efficient Medical Diagnosis of Human Heart Diseases Using Machine Learning Techniques With and Without GridSearchCV," IEEE Access, vol. 10, pp. 80151-80173, 2022. doi: 10.1109/ACCESS.2022.3165792
**Dataset:** Cleveland, Statlog and a Kaggle heart dataset
**Technique:** SVM, KNN, DT, RF, LR, NB and boosting with and without grid search
**Reported result:** Tuned RF and SVM close to 99% on some splits
**Summary:** Ahmad et al. isolated the effect of hyperparameter tuning by running every model twice, once with defaults and once with GridSearchCV, on three datasets.

**Relevance to this project:** Shows how much tuning inflates single split numbers; our study intentionally uses default or lightly set hyperparameters so the ensemble effect is not confounded with tuning.
[20] Grey wolf optimized stacked ensemble for early heart disease prediction (2024)

**Full reference:** G. Narasimhan and A. Victor, "Grey wolf optimized stacked ensemble machine learning based model for enhanced efficiency and reliability of predicting early heart disease," Automatika, vol. 65, no. 3, pp. 749-762, 2024. doi: 10.1080/00051144.2024.2317098
**Dataset:** Heart patient dataset
**Technique:** Stacked ensemble whose hyperparameters are chosen by Grey Wolf Optimization
**Reported result:** Reported improvement over unoptimized stacking
**Summary:** Narasimhan and Victor combined a metaheuristic optimizer with stacking so that base learner settings and the meta learner are optimized together.
**Relevance to this project:** Represents the current trend of optimizer plus ensemble hybrids; a natural future extension of our Stacking model.
[21] Ensemble learning with explainable AI for heart disease prediction (IELF) (2025)

**Full reference:** A. Adekoya, F. Saeed, W. Ghaban and S. N. Qasem, "Ensemble learning approach with explainable AI for improved heart disease prediction," Frontiers in Pharmacology, vol. 16, art. 1654681, 2025. doi: 10.3389/fphar.2025.1654681
**Dataset:** Framingham and other heart datasets
**Technique:** Soft voting of XGBoost and Explainable Boosting Machine with nested CV, SHAP and LIME
**Reported result:** Reports calibrated, leakage controlled results with confidence intervals

**Summary:** Adekoya et al. argue that many published accuracies above 97% come from leakage or optimistic protocols, and they use nested cross validation and train only resampling to obtain honest estimates.
**Relevance to this project:** Supports the central observation of our project: the 95.33% of the base paper is not reproducible under a leakage free protocol, while the ensemble ranking still holds.
